messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed an ~8-12% perf regression on long-context Llama2-13B runs after landing the fused RoPE change into flashattn3. Nightly bench on devcluster-gpu-pool.
kevin: Can you paste the exact bench command + kernel variant + any env flags? which kv/cache policy were you using?
sasha: Also, did the patch change any batching heuristics? I've seen the adaptive packer fall back to single-turn path when certain flags toggle.
maria: Command I used: `./bench_runner --model llama2-13b --kernel flashattn3-fusedrope --seq 8192 --batch 1 --kv_cache paged --quant none --profile > out.log`
kevin: thx. quick guess: kernel selection might be picking a slower matmul path when rotary dims / strides change. can you drop the raw out.log?
maria: Pasted summary: tokens/sec 920 vs baseline 1000, p95 latency +18%. stack shows extra memcpy in ropemap_apply -> flash_kernel_dispatch.
lee: I profiled memory churn: KV eviction rate up ~20% and tail-latency spikes coincide with large memcpy windows. small sample: eviction_count went from 12->15 per minute, memcpy bytes +30%.
infra-bot: buildbot: benchmark job 1732507001 finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/bench/1732507001/summary.json
kevin: can you try `rope_scale_dims=false` in runtime config and/or `kernel=flashattn3-fusedrope-no-prefetch` if that build exists? trying to isolate prefetch vs rope transform interaction.
sasha: I tried `flashattn3-fusedrope-no-prefetch` locally — tokens/sec recovered to within ~2% of baseline but latency variance increased. suggests prefetch + kv cache interplay.
lee: microbench snapshot I ran: ```python
# quick harness
run_bench(kernel='flashattn3-fusedrope', seq=8192, kv_policy='paged', batch_policy='adaptive')
``` results: 920 tok/s (baseline 1000 tok/s). added kv_eviction counter: +20% evictions.
kevin: can someone run a kernel-only matmul microbench across rotary_dim_scale {0.5,1.0,1.5}? suspect stride/packing change causing kernel_selector to choose a fallback.
maria: Good call — I'll try to get a minimal reproducer. If it's a selector heuristic, bisect should be fast.
sasha: quick find: when rotary_dim_scale != 1.0 our fast-path assumes contiguous rotary dims; stride calc changes and the selector in kernel_selector.cpp picks the slower generic matmul. patch idea: add a stride-aware fastpath check. PR draft incoming.
kevin: I'll run a perf bisect on nightly and post the commit that introduced the regression. also checking whether paged-KV page-size interacts with memcpy pattern.
lee: Note: if we need an immediate mitigation, setting `kernel_override=flashattn3-v1` on dedicated pool restores perf to baseline in my tests.
infra-bot: incident-bot: perf-alert created: PERF-2026-041 by maria. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PERF-2026-041
maria: thanks all. plan: kevin bisect + post logs, sasha PR for stride-aware selector, lee run kv eviction microbench with different page sizes, i'll attach repro artifacts here when ready. :thumbsup:
kevin: assigned to me. will update thread when bisect finds culprit.
sasha: PR opened for selector check, tagging kevin for validation. short description in PR: "check rotary_dim_stride and fallback only if non-optimal".
maria: if kevin confirms selector is root cause we'll ship a narrow revert or selector patch. otherwise we may roll back fused-rope flag.
lee: I pushed a small benchmark artifact to s3: s3://redwood-perf-temp/fusedrope/1732507099/microbench.tar.gz
maria: I'll attach the out.log and flamegraph here after I scrub customer data. thanks everyone.
